assessment: Kovacs et al. provide important and valuable data on the role of meningeal lymphatic drainage in T cell responses during chronic Toxoplasma gondii (T.g.) infection in mice. They present compelling data showing dendritic cell (DC) accumulation in the dura and CSF at 6 weeks post-infection, which matches with the replication peak of T.g. in the brain, and with T cell expansion/activation in the draining lymph node (dCLN). They also convincingly show that during chronic infection, antigen-specific T cells are generated not only in the dCLN but also in the periphery (ILN), which could account for the presence of T cells in the brain after surgical blockade of the lymphatics. This study highlights also how the CNS is protected against environmental challenges.
